result.title: CHORD: Multi-resolution Compression for Multimodal Time Series
result.summary: Wearables, mobile devices, and IoT platforms generate multimodal time-series data continuously and at scale, making efficient storage and transfer a primary concern. The same recordings are reused after collection by many downstream models, often at different temporal resolutions, so a compressed representation should be small, useful across resolutions, and produced at a bit rate known in advance. Prior work meets parts of this: symbolic and error-bounded compressors reconstruct accurately but fix resolution at compression time, learned codecs target one signal domain, and discrete tokenizers reconstruct without accounting for rate. We introduce CHORD, a coarse-to-fine compressor for heterogeneous multimodal time series. A residual cascade orders each payload from broad to fine temporal scales and synthesizes corrections through learned shapelet-inspired atoms. A shared pathway supplies a reusable synthesis basis across modalities, while private pathways retain capacity for sensor-specific morphology. Finite scalar quantization fixes the bit width of every modality and scale, so payload size is known before encoding, and scale dropout trains each coarse-to-fine prefix to be a valid reconstruction operating point. Across seven wearable-sensing and forecasting benchmarks, CHORD stays within 0.62 points of uncompressed classification accuracy on average at the 8x target, the smallest gap of any compressed method, with all resolutions decoded from one payload.

AI.brief_summary: CHORD 提出一种由粗到细的多模态可穿戴时间序列压缩器，用残差级联与有限标量量化实现固定比特率、单一载荷多分辨率重建。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是面向存储与传输的传感器数据压缩，评价聚焦重构与分类精度，不涉及视觉证据的保留、推理状态生成或停止决策；虽然「多模态」「量化」「前缀即有效重建点」与 latent 预算或任意时刻解码有表面相似，但材料中并无可供核查的具体方法线索，故不入选。
